SMTO-API-0011 — API validation failed

GUID: aeb5e76b-6969-4bc3-96bf-550068af7df4
Slug: api-validation-failed
Domain: API · Subsystem: api

What happened

  • SMTO couldn't use a value sent from this page, such as a search filter, a name or an option. When it can, this panel lists which value to fix.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Check the Fields to correct list in this panel and change each listed value to what its description asks for. Those lines name the values SMTO rejected; what you typed isn't shown there, to keep it private.
  2. If you were searching or filtering conversations, select Clear search (the × in the search box), reset the filters, and choose them again. A filter saved by an older version of the page can hold a value SMTO no longer accepts.
  3. Reload this page, then repeat the action once. A page left open across an SMTO update can send options in an older form.

What success looks like

  • The search, filter or change is accepted without this message.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO, noting what you were doing. Don't keep sending the same value; it will be rejected the same way.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • An SMTO or Gateway validator rejected the request with HTTP 422 (for example an unknown conversation sort, status or task-type filter, an invalid approval_mode, or a malformed Gateway job-event cursor), or an otherwise unclassified 422 was returned.

What this means

  • API validators reject unsupported task types, approval modes or malformed event-stream cursors; generic status 422 also maps here when no specific cause exists. Generic API status and exception families establish only their stated boundary. Stronger structured causes take precedence; the original receipt determines whether work started or had effects, and diagnostics add no dispatch or retry.

Why this can happen

  • API validators reject unsupported task types, approval modes or malformed event-stream cursors; generic status 422 also maps here when no specific cause exists.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect safe field/constraint details and the actual route rather than submitted private values.

How to fix it

  • Use the field issues in Technical details (submitted values are intentionally omitted) to correct the request: valid conversation sorts are recent, oldest, title and best_match; task_type filters are normal and scheduled; approval_mode is manual or full_access. Clear stale saved UI filter state and reload outdated clients.
  • Correct the named fields and constraints; invalid supplied values are omitted from public diagnostics.

Retry and execution caution

  • Apply the correction and confirm the relevant state before requesting another attempt. Prior completed work remains governed by its receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • Correctly typed bounded fields pass the intended route's validation.

What not to do

  • Do not repeatedly submit the same invalid input; correct the named constraint first.

Technical notes

  • Generic API status and exception families establish only their stated boundary. Stronger structured causes take precedence; the original receipt determines whether work started or had effects, and diagnostics add no dispatch or retry.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
